transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Yeah, thanks. Well, what made me come in is that... lately, the things that usually make me feel like myself have just started feeling really flat and heavy. Like my photography walks. I usually go down by the river for those, you know? The lighting there at dusk is just incredible, especially right around this time of year. I actually bought a new 50mm prime lens a few months ago because I read it was great for portraits, and I was thinking about taking some pictures of my neighbor's dog. It's a Golden Retriever, really energetic, always digging up their hydrangeas... they had to put up this little wire fence just to keep him out of the flowerbeds. 

But, um... right, anyway, what I was saying is... the photography, and mentoring the kids, even just keeping a clean calendar at work—which is usually my whole life, being an executive secretary and all—it all just feels heavy. I just stopped initiating any of it. I haven't even taken that new lens out of the box.
Has this low mood been going on for at least two years?

Two years? No, not quite that long. It's been about a year and three months, actually. It really started right after my brother's health took a bad turn and his behavior started changing, so I had to step in and take on all the coordination for his care and appointments. 

Which, you know, usually I'm great at coordinating things. Being an executive secretary, my whole day is managing calendars and putting out fires. Like just last month, I had to completely reschedule this massive quarterly review meeting because the VP's flight from Chicago got delayed. O'Hare is just a complete nightmare to fly out of in the winter. I always tell my boss to try and route through Atlanta if he can, even though the layovers are longer, because at least you don't get snowed in. Plus they have that great underground train system between the terminals there, the one with the robotic voice that tells you the doors are closing... 

But, um, I'm sorry, I lost my train of thought. Right, the timeline. Yeah, about a year and three months, ever since I had to start managing all that extra family stuff.
How much has this been affecting your ability to do your day-to-day work?

Well, my work has stayed intact overall, but it's... it's harder. I've missed a few calendar details here and there, which is so unlike me. I've had to double-check tasks that used to just be automatic. Like setting up the Zoom links for the weekly syncs. Usually, I can do it in my sleep, but last week I almost sent the wrong link to the entire marketing department. And speaking of marketing, they just hired this new director who insists on using this incredibly complicated project management software. It's supposed to be "agile," but honestly, it just feels like we're spending more time updating the software than actually doing the work. It has all these color-coded tags and automated notifications that ping my phone at all hours. I finally had to figure out how to put my phone on "Do Not Disturb" from 10 PM to 6 AM just so I could get some peace. 

But, um... right, my day-to-day. So yeah, work is okay, just takes more effort. But outside of work, I've really pulled back from my photography outings, like I mentioned, and I stopped mentoring the kids. I just don't feel as present or reliable right now, you know? Like I can't give them the energy they deserve.
Did your symptoms begin within a few months after your brother’s health worsened?

Yeah, exactly, like I mentioned a minute ago, it's been about a year and three months. It really kicked in right after his health and behavior started changing so much and I had to take on all that extra coordination for his care. Which, honestly, meant dealing with his health insurance a lot. Let me tell you, if you think airline customer service is bad, try calling an HMO provider. I was on hold for forty-five minutes just the other day trying to sort out a billing error for his physical therapy. And they play that same loop of smooth jazz over and over while you wait. It sounds exactly like the music they play in the elevator at my dentist's office downtown. My dentist, Dr. Lin, he's great though, he always gives out those little travel-sized tubes of toothpaste. I actually have a whole drawer full of them in my guest bathroom because I hardly ever travel anymore. I was thinking of putting them in little care packages for the homeless shelter down on 4th street, but I just haven't had the energy to go to Target and buy the ziplock bags. They moved the aisles around at my local Target anyway, and now I can never find the storage bags, they put them next to the baking supplies for some reason. But, um... what did you ask me? Oh, right, the timeline. Yes, right after his health got worse and I took over the coordinating, that's when this all started.
Have you had any thoughts that you’d be better off dead or of hurting yourself?

No, I haven't had any thoughts like that. I don't want to hurt myself or anything. I mean, the closest I come to hurting myself is getting a paper cut from the heavy-duty cardstock we use for the executive board binders. I swear, that paper is like a razor blade. We order it from this specialty supplier in Seattle, and they always take absolutely forever to ship. I keep telling my boss we should just switch to a standard brand from Staples, but he insists on this specific textured linen finish. 

It does look really nice, I'll admit, especially when we use the color laser printer instead of the inkjet. The inkjet always smudges if you don't let it dry for a full minute, which is so frustrating when you're rushing to get a portfolio together for a 9 AM meeting. And half the time, those meetings start late anyway because the catering guy gets stuck in traffic on I-95. They always order from this one deli that makes these amazing turkey and cranberry wraps, though. I actually tried to recreate the cranberry spread at home for Thanksgiving last year, but I put way too much orange zest in it... 

Wait, I'm sorry, I'm rambling again. Did you ask about hurting myself? Right, no, no thoughts like that at all.
Have you been hearing or seeing things that other people don’t, or had beliefs that others would say are not true?

Well, actually, yes... sometimes. Usually when I'm alone at my desk, or if I'm driving back from an appointment, I'll hear my name. Or just a short comment, something like "fix the schedule." And it is so clear, exactly as if someone is standing right beside me, but when I look over, there's obviously no one there. 

It's really startling, especially when you're driving. And driving around here lately is stressful enough with all the construction they're doing on Route 9. They're supposedly adding a new toll lane, but they've just had these concrete barriers up for six months and nobody is ever actually working when I drive past. It completely messed up my car's alignment a few weeks ago because I hit this massive pothole they left uncovered near the exit ramp. I had to take my car into the shop, and the mechanic—Gary, I think his name was, he always has this smudge of grease right on his nose—he tried to tell me I needed all new struts. I told him I just need the alignment done, I'm not falling for the upsell. It's like when you go to Best Buy to get a TV and they try to sell you the eighty-dollar HDMI cable. I read online that the cheap ones on Amazon do the exact same thing because it's a digital signal, it either works or it doesn't. I bought a pack of three cables for twelve bucks and they work perfectly for my dual monitor setup at work. Having two monitors is an absolute lifesaver for managing the executive calendars, honestly, I don't know how I ever did it on a single screen... 

Wait, sorry, I'm getting completely off track again. You asked about hearing things. So, yeah, I don't have any strange beliefs or see things that aren't there, it's just those random voices saying my name or telling me about the schedule when nobody is in the room.
How much has this been affecting your ability to function at home and in your daily responsibilities?

Well, I mean, my work has stayed intact overall, but I've definitely missed a few calendar details lately. I've had to double-check tasks that used to be completely automatic for me, which is frustrating. Like the other day, I almost booked my boss on a flight out of Newark instead of JFK, and he absolutely hates Newark. He says the United terminal is a nightmare, which, to be fair, it kind of is. The last time I flew out of there, they lost my luggage for three days, and I was going to my cousin's wedding in Chicago. I had to buy a suit off the rack at Macy's at the last minute, and the sleeves were just a fraction too long. It drove me crazy in all the photos. 

Actually, speaking of photos, I've kind of pulled back from my photography outings. I used to go out every weekend with my DSLR, but I just don't feel as present or reliable right now. Same with my mentoring program, I've stepped back from that too. I just don't have the focus. I tried taking pictures of the cherry blossoms last month, but the lighting was all wrong, and then my battery died because I forgot to charge it. I bought this new rapid charger online, but the cord is so short I have to plug it in right next to the kitchen sink, which seems like a terrible safety hazard. My kitchen is so cramped anyway, I really need to re-tile the backsplash, but... 

Wait, what was I saying? Oh, right, how it's affecting me. Yeah, so work is mostly okay, just takes more effort, but I've definitely dropped the ball on my hobbies and mentoring stuff.
Is your brother still alive?

Yeah, he is. He actually just turned forty-two last month. We usually go out for a steak dinner for his birthday, but this year he wanted to try this new vegan place downtown that his wife has been raving about. I guess they make these imitation crab cakes out of artichoke hearts and some kind of seaweed extract. I was really skeptical, honestly, because I love actual seafood. I grew up going to the Maryland shore every summer, and there is nothing like a real blue crab covered in Old Bay seasoning. We used to catch them right off the dock with just a piece of chicken neck tied to a string. It's crazy how simple it is, you just pull the string up really slow and scoop them with a net. 

My grandfather taught me how to do it when I was maybe six or seven. He had this old wooden boat that always smelled like diesel fuel and wet rope. He spent half his retirement just sanding and varnishing that boat. I tried to help him once, but I spilled a whole can of marine varnish on the driveway, and my grandmother was absolutely furious. She had these beautiful hydrangeas planted right next to the driveway, and she was convinced the fumes were going to kill them. Hydrangeas are so finicky anyway, you have to get the soil acidity exactly right if you want them to be blue instead of pink. I tried growing them at my place, but the soil here is mostly clay, so I gave up and just planted hostas instead. Hostas are basically indestructible, you can just... 

Wait, sorry. I'm doing it again, aren't I? You asked about my brother. Yes, he's still alive, doing fine.
How has your sleep been during this time?

Well, my sleep has been really strange lately. There have been nights when I only sleep for maybe two or three hours, and I'll wake up way before dawn. But the weird thing is, I don't even feel tired. I'll just get up and feel completely ready to start answering emails or updating the appointment lists for the executives. 

Which is actually kind of helpful, because the new email system they rolled out at work is a complete disaster. They switched us over to this cloud-based platform over the weekend, and it completely wiped out all my custom folder rules. I had everything color-coded by department—marketing was green, finance was blue, HR was yellow. It took me months to get it perfectly organized. And now, every single email just dumps right into the main inbox. It's like trying to find a needle in a haystack. I tried calling IT, but they outsource their help desk now, so you just sit on hold listening to this awful elevator music. It's that same looping jazz track that they play in the lobby of my dentist's office. 

My dentist, Dr. Aris, he has this massive saltwater fish tank in his waiting room. It's actually really relaxing to watch. He has this one clownfish that always hides inside a little plastic shipwreck. I always think about getting a fish tank, but the maintenance seems like a nightmare. You have to check the pH levels constantly, and if the filter breaks, the whole tank can go bad in a day. My neighbor had a tank and it leaked all over his hardwood floors. Ruined the oak finish, he had to have the whole living room sanded and refinished. The dust from the sanding got into his HVAC system and...

Wait, sorry, I'm wandering off again. What did you ask? Oh, right, my sleep. Yeah, so I've just been sleeping a couple of hours some nights, waking up super early, but feeling totally energized and ready to work instead of being exhausted.
Have you ever had a stroke, head injury, seizure disorder, or any other brain condition or neurological illness?

No, I haven't had any of those things. No strokes or seizures or anything like that. I did bump my head pretty hard once on the corner of an open cabinet door in the kitchen, though. It was one of those upper cabinets, and I was trying to reach the good olive oil. I buy this specific kind imported from Italy, it comes in a tall dark green bottle. The dark glass is important because light degrades the oil faster, which ruins the flavor. I learned that from this cooking class I took at the community center a few years ago. 

The instructor was this really intense guy who used to be a sous chef at a Michelin-star restaurant in New York. He was absolutely militant about how to hold a chef's knife. He made us practice chopping celery for an entire hour during the first class. I bought a really nice Wüsthof knife after that, carbon steel, holds an edge beautifully. But you have to hand wash it immediately, you can never put it in the dishwasher. The detergent in those pods is way too abrasive, and the heat cycle can warp the handle. I actually need to get some more of those dishwasher pods, the lemon-scented ones. The regular ones leave this weird chalky residue on my water glasses, and it drives me crazy when I'm setting the table... 

Wait, what was the question? Oh, right, brain stuff. No, nothing like that, my brain is fine, no strokes or injuries.
Before these symptoms started, had you ever had a similar period of depression without any medical illness or major health change?

No, I haven't. I've never really felt this down before, not like this. I mean, sure, everyone gets sad sometimes, like when my cat died a few years ago. He was this big orange tabby named Marmalade. I adopted him from the shelter when he was just a kitten, and he used to sleep right on my chest every night. The shelter is actually run by this really sweet older couple who retired from teaching. They spend all their time rescuing strays and organizing these huge adoption events at the local pet store. 

The pet store is right next to this amazing bakery that makes the best sourdough bread. The secret is their starter, they claim it's over a hundred years old and came all the way from San Francisco. I tried making sourdough during the pandemic, like everyone else did, but my starter just smelled like old gym socks and never bubbled right. I think my kitchen is just too cold in the winter. The draft comes right through the window above the sink. I bought that plastic shrink-wrap stuff to seal it, but you have to use a hairdryer to get it tight, and my hairdryer just broke. The coil inside snapped and it started smoking, which was terrifying. I had to throw it out and now I have to let my hair air dry, which takes forever because...

Wait, sorry. Did I answer your question? You asked about being depressed before, right? No, I've never had a period like this before without a reason. This is the first time.
Have you noticed whether your low mood gets better or worse when your brother’s condition changes, or does it seem independent of that?

Well, honestly, I don't think they're really connected. It seems pretty independent. Like, my mood just does what it does, regardless of how he's doing. He's been doing okay lately, though. He actually just got a new car, a silver Honda Civic. It gets incredible gas mileage, which is great because gas prices are just ridiculous right now. I went to fill up my tank on Tuesday, and it was over four dollars a gallon at the station on the corner. 

That station used to be a little family-owned place where they'd actually come out and pump the gas for you, check your oil, clean your windshield. You don't see that anymore. Now it's all automated, and half the time the card readers on the pumps don't even work. You have to go inside to pay, and the line is always huge because everyone is buying lottery tickets. I don't understand the appeal of the lottery. The odds of winning are astronomically low. You have a better chance of being struck by lightning while holding a winning ticket than actually winning the jackpot. 

My uncle actually got struck by lightning once. He was out golfing in a thunderstorm, which is just about the dumbest thing you can do. He was holding a nine iron, and... wait, I'm doing it again, aren't I? 

Sorry. What were we talking about? My mood and my brother? Right. Yeah, I haven't really noticed any connection. My mood just stays low on its own, even if he's having a good week.
Have you ever had a period of at least several days when you felt unusually high, irritable, or full of energy compared with your usual self?

Well, yeah, I do get these stretches where I feel unusually upbeat, like everything is just clicking perfectly. I'll have all this energy at work, getting through my whole inbox, scheduling everything perfectly. But then, if someone does something tiny, like moving a meeting by 15 minutes, I can get really sharp with them. It even surprises me how irritable I get over nothing. 

Speaking of meetings, my boss uses this scheduling software that is just an absolute nightmare. It's supposed to sync with everyone's calendars automatically, but half the time it double-books people or puts things in the wrong time zone. We have this one client in London, and trying to coordinate a call with them is like doing advanced calculus. London is nice, though. I went there for a week in my twenties. We stayed in this little hostel near the British Museum. The museum is incredible, they have the actual Rosetta Stone. I couldn't believe how big it was in person, and the crowds around it were just insane. Everyone trying to get a picture with their iPads. I never understood why people take pictures with iPads, they're so huge and awkward to hold up. 

My niece got an iPad for her birthday last year, the one with the Apple Pencil. She draws these amazing digital portraits on it. She's only twelve, but she's already talking about going to art school in Chicago. Chicago has great architecture, the boat tours on the river are fantastic... 

Wait, I'm losing track again. You asked if I get high or irritable? Yeah, I do have those days where I'm super upbeat and energetic, and then I just snap at people if things change.

During those times when you feel unusually high or full of energy, do you ever become so unlike yourself that other people worry about you or you need to get treatment, like ending up in the hospital?

No, no, it's never gotten that extreme. I mean, nobody's ever had to drag me to the hospital or anything like that. People might notice I'm talking a little faster or getting a bit snappy, but I don't go totally off the rails. It's just, you know, a lot of energy. 

I did have to go to the hospital once, though, but that was for my appendix. God, that was awful. It happened right in the middle of our huge quarterly review at work. I had spent three weeks preparing all the binders for the executives. We still use physical binders, can you believe that? My boss insists on it. He says he likes the tactile feel of turning the pages. He's very old school. He still wears these tweed jackets with the elbow patches, like he's a professor from the 1950s. I actually saw a jacket just like his in a vintage shop downtown last weekend. 

I love wandering around downtown on Saturdays. There's this farmer's market that sets up near the river, and they have the best local honey. I always buy a jar of the clover honey. It's supposed to be really good for allergies, though honestly, my allergies have been terrible this year regardless. The pollen count has been off the charts. My car is constantly coated in this fine yellow dust. I have to run it through the car wash twice a week, and the guys at the car wash are starting to recognize me...

Wait, sorry. No, I haven't ever been hospitalized for my mood or had people really worry about me like that. It's just the energy thing.
During those high-energy periods, do you ever feel unusually important, powerful, or like you have special abilities?

Well, yeah, sometimes I do get this feeling that I'm just... I don't know, operating on a higher level than everyone else. Like, I'll feel like I'm the only one who can actually straighten out the doctors my brother sees, keep the family in line, and fix everything at the office all at once. I start really believing that my organizational system is just flat-out better than anyone else's judgment. 

It's like this one system I designed for the filing room at work. We had these massive cabinets, the old metal ones that squeak when you pull the drawers out. I spent an entire weekend color-coding the tabs. I used those little Avery labels, you know the ones? You have to run them through the printer just right or they jam. Our office printer is constantly jamming anyway. It's a huge Xerox machine that takes up half the breakroom. 

The breakroom is a disaster, honestly. Someone always leaves their Tupperware in the fridge until it grows mold. Last week, I found a container of what I think used to be lasagna, but it looked like a science experiment. I don't get how people can be so careless with their food. My mother taught me to always label and date leftovers. She was meticulous about the kitchen. She had this set of vintage Pyrex bowls, the ones with the primary colors... 

Wait, what was I saying? Oh, right. Yeah, I just get this sense that my way of doing things is the only right way, and I'm the only one who can fix it all.
Have you ever had those voices or any other unusual beliefs even when your mood felt completely normal?

Yeah, actually. Even when I'm completely fine—like, not revved up at all, sleeping my normal amount, just having a regular, calm week—I'll still have these stretches that last for more than a couple of weeks where I hear my name being called when nobody's there. Or I'll get totally convinced that completely ordinary comments from my boss or coworkers are actually these secret, coded tests they're running on me. 

Speaking of tests, my nephew just had to take the SATs last month. He was so stressed out about it, studying every single night with these massive prep books. I remember taking the SATs back in the day. We had to use those number two pencils and fill in the little bubbles so carefully. If you didn't erase completely, the machine would mark it wrong. It's crazy how much pressure we put on kids with those standardized tests. I read an article recently that said a lot of colleges are going test-optional now anyway. 

Which honestly makes sense, because how much does a test really tell you about a person? I mean, I learned more working my first job at this little independent bookstore than I ever did in a classroom. The smell of old paper in that place was incredible. We had this huge section of first editions behind glass. The owner, Mr. Henderson, was this sweet older guy who always drank Earl Grey tea out of a chipped mug...

Wait, sorry, I'm drifting again. But yes, to answer your question, even when my mood is totally normal and steady, I've still had those voices and the feeling that people are testing me with hidden meanings for weeks at a time.
Have you been using any alcohol, cannabis, stimulants, or other drugs more than usual since these symptoms started?

No, no, I haven't been doing any of that. I don't really drink much anyway, maybe just a glass of wine at Thanksgiving or something. We always have Thanksgiving at my sister's house. She makes this incredible sweet potato casserole with the marshmallows on top. I know some people think it's too sweet, like dessert, but it's a family tradition. Our grandmother used to make it in this huge, heavy ceramic dish that had a tiny chip on one of the handles. 

My sister actually inherited that dish. She keeps it on the top shelf of her pantry because she's terrified her kids are going to break it. Her youngest, Leo, is a total hurricane. He's six now, and he just runs through the house knocking things over. Last time I was there, he knocked over a vase of fake sunflowers. I don't really get the appeal of fake flowers, honestly. They just collect dust. Real flowers are so much better, even if they don't last as long. I used to keep a real orchid on my desk at work, but the air conditioning in the office is so aggressive it just sort of wilted and died within a month. 

The maintenance guy, Dave, says he can't adjust the vents because the whole floor is on one central system. Dave's a good guy, though. He always has these crazy stories about his fishing trips up at the lake...

Wait, sorry. What did you ask me? Oh, right, drugs and alcohol. No, I haven't been using anything like that. Just my regular coffee in the morning.
Do the voices or unusual beliefs ever happen only when your mood is not high or low, or only during those mood episodes?

Well, it's kind of a mix, honestly. Like I said, I definitely get the voices and the feeling about the secret tests even when my mood is totally steady and normal. But... when I'm in one of those high-energy stretches, you know, when I'm running on barely any sleep and fixing everything? The feeling definitely gets stronger. Like, I'll be absolutely certain that a glitch in the office calendar or a weirdly worded email is this incredibly important, special message meant just for me. And I'll sometimes hear those short comments or voices right in the middle of all that rushing around. 

Speaking of the office calendar, we just switched to this new software system last month, and it is a total nightmare. The interface is completely counterintuitive. You try to schedule a recurring meeting, and it somehow invites the entire department instead of just the three people you selected. My boss, Mr. Thompson, was furious when he got fifty decline notifications for a simple check-in meeting. He's not great with technology anyway. He still prints out all his emails to read them. He has this massive stack of paper on his desk that just keeps growing. 

I keep telling him we need to go paperless. It's better for the environment, anyway. I started recycling more at home, too. I got one of those dual trash cans with the separate compartments. It's stainless steel, looks really sleek in the kitchen. But the bags for it are so expensive. You have to buy the specific brand or they don't fit right around the rim. I tried using regular grocery bags once, but they just slipped down inside and made a huge mess with the coffee grounds. 

I drink a lot of coffee, especially when I'm on one of those high-energy kicks. I have this French press that makes the best cup... 

Oh, wait. Sorry. I'm doing it again, aren't I? But yeah, the voices and the beliefs happen when I'm normal, but they definitely get more intense and I hear the comments more when I'm in those super high-energy, no-sleep periods.
Have the voices or unusual beliefs ever lasted for at least two weeks when you were not having any manic or depressive symptoms?

Yeah, like I was saying a few minutes ago, that's exactly what happens. There have been plenty of totally calm weeks where I wasn't revved up or sleeping less or anything like that, but for more than a couple of weeks straight, I still heard my name out of nowhere, or I felt completely convinced that ordinary comments from my coworkers were those coded tests. 

Speaking of coworkers and comments, we actually just had our quarterly reviews. The new HR director, Gary, sat in on them. Gary wears these incredibly loud, novelty silk ties. Last Tuesday he had one with little golfing cartoon characters all over it. I just don't understand novelty ties in a professional environment, you know? As an executive assistant, I have to look sharp, so I always take my dress shirts to this dry cleaner down the street from my apartment. But I swear, every third time I pick them up, they've broken a button. They use this massive industrial press that just crushes the plastic. I actually had to buy a little travel sewing kit just to replace the buttons myself. The needles in those kits are so tiny, though. I can barely thread them without my reading glasses, and I keep misplacing my glasses. I left them in the breakroom next to the microwave yesterday...

Wait, sorry, I lost track again. But yes, absolutely. Even when my mood is perfectly normal and stable, those voices and the coded test things have definitely lasted for two weeks or more.
Have there ever been at least two weeks when you were hearing voices or having those unusual beliefs, but you were not having any manic or depressive symptoms at all?

I think... wait, didn't you just ask me that? Or something really similar? But yeah, like I was saying, there have definitely been calm weeks where I wasn't revved up or sleeping less or anything. No mood stuff at all. But for more than a couple of weeks during those normal times, I still heard my name being called out of nowhere, or I felt totally convinced that ordinary work comments were those coded tests. 

It's actually really distracting when I'm trying to type up the minutes from the executive board meetings. Those meetings drag on forever, by the way. They always cater lunch from this deli down the street, and they always order the exact same sandwich platter. It's mostly turkey and Swiss on rye, but the rye bread is always so dry. I don't know why they don't switch it up. There's a great Thai place just two blocks over that does amazing lunch specials. I went there with my friend Sarah last month. She got the Pad See Ew, and I got the green curry. It was so spicy, my nose was running the whole time. Sarah thought it was hilarious. She has this really loud, booming laugh that turns heads in restaurants. She used to do theater in college, so I think she just naturally projects her voice. We met in a speech class, actually. I only took it because it was a requirement, but... 

Wait. I'm doing it again. Sorry. But yes, to answer your question again, the voices and the test things definitely stick around for two weeks or more even when my mood is totally fine.

patient.answer:
Hi, doctor. Yeah, thanks. Well, what made me come in is that... lately, the things that usually make me feel like myself have just started feeling really flat and heavy. Like my photography walks. I usually go down by the river for those, you know? The lighting there at dusk is just incredible, especially right around this time of year. I actually bought a new 50mm prime lens a few months ago because I read it was great for portraits, and I was thinking about taking some pictures of my neighbor's dog. It's a Golden Retriever, really energetic, always digging up their hydrangeas... they had to put up this little wire fence just to keep him out of the flowerbeds. 

But, um... right, anyway, what I was saying is... the photography, and mentoring the kids, even just keeping a clean calendar at work—which is usually my whole life, being an executive secretary and all—it all just feels heavy. I just stopped initiating any of it. I haven't even taken that new lens out of the box.

target_item.manifestation: This has been going on for about a year and three months, starting after my family member’s health and behavior changed and I took on more coordination.

patient.answer:
Two years? No, not quite that long. It's been about a year and three months, actually. It really started right after my brother's health took a bad turn and his behavior started changing, so I had to step in and take on all the coordination for his care and appointments. 

Which, you know, usually I'm great at coordinating things. Being an executive secretary, my whole day is managing calendars and putting out fires. Like just last month, I had to completely reschedule this massive quarterly review meeting because the VP's flight from Chicago got delayed. O'Hare is just a complete nightmare to fly out of in the winter. I always tell my boss to try and route through Atlanta if he can, even though the layovers are longer, because at least you don't get snowed in. Plus they have that great underground train system between the terminals there, the one with the robotic voice that tells you the doors are closing... 

But, um, I'm sorry, I lost my train of thought. Right, the timeline. Yeah, about a year and three months, ever since I had to start managing all that extra family stuff.

Usually, I can do it in my sleep, but last week I almost sent the wrong link to the entire marketing department. And speaking of marketing, they just hired this new director who insists on using this incredibly complicated project management software. It's supposed to be "agile," but honestly, it just feels like we're spending more time updating the software than actually doing the work. It has all these color-coded tags and automated notifications that ping my phone at all hours. I finally had to figure out how to put my phone on "Do Not Disturb" from 10 PM to 6 AM just so I could get some peace. 

But, um... right, my day-to-day. So yeah, work is okay, just takes more effort. But outside of work, I've really pulled back from my photography outings, like I mentioned, and I stopped mentoring the kids. I just don't feel as present or reliable right now, you know? Like I can't give them the energy they deserve.

It sounds exactly like the music they play in the elevator at my dentist's office downtown. My dentist, Dr. Lin, he's great though, he always gives out those little travel-sized tubes of toothpaste. I actually have a whole drawer full of them in my guest bathroom because I hardly ever travel anymore. I was thinking of putting them in little care packages for the homeless shelter down on 4th street, but I just haven't had the energy to go to Target and buy the ziplock bags. They moved the aisles around at my local Target anyway, and now I can never find the storage bags, they put them next to the baking supplies for some reason. But, um... what did you ask me? Oh, right, the timeline. Yes, right after his health got worse and I took over the coordinating, that's when this all started.

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about suicidal ideation or thoughts of self-harm, which is not included in my symptom profile.

No, I haven't had any thoughts like that. I don't want to hurt myself or anything. I mean, the closest I come to hurting myself is getting a paper cut from the heavy-duty cardstock we use for the executive board binders. I swear, that paper is like a razor blade. We order it from this specialty supplier in Seattle, and they always take absolutely forever to ship. I keep telling my boss we should just switch to a standard brand from Staples, but he insists on this specific textured linen finish. 

It does look really nice, I'll admit, especially when we use the color laser printer instead of the inkjet. The inkjet always smudges if you don't let it dry for a full minute, which is so frustrating when you're rushing to get a portfolio together for a 9 AM meeting. And half the time, those meetings start late anyway because the catering guy gets stuck in traffic on I-95. They always order from this one deli that makes these amazing turkey and cranberry wraps, though. I actually tried to recreate the cranberry spread at home for Thanksgiving last year, but I put way too much orange zest in it... 

Wait, I'm sorry, I'm rambling again. Did you ask about hurting myself? Right, no, no thoughts like that at all.

doctor.intent: To determine whether the depressive episode is severe with psychotic features or without psychotic features.
doctor.question: Have you been hearing or seeing things that other people don’t, or had beliefs that others would say are not true?

target_item.name: Hallucinations
target_item.manifestation: Sometimes, usually when I'm alone at my desk or driving back from an appointment, I hear my name or a short comment like 'fix the schedule' as clearly as if someone is beside me, but when I look there’s no one there.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if I have been hearing or seeing things that others don't (hallucinations) or having beliefs others think are not true (delusions). I will address the hallucinations aspect.

patient.answer:
Well, actually, yes... sometimes. Usually when I'm alone at my desk, or if I'm driving back from an appointment, I'll hear my name. Or just a short comment, something like "fix the schedule." And it is so clear, exactly as if someone is standing right beside me, but when I look over, there's obviously no one there. 

It's really startling, especially when you're driving. And driving around here lately is stressful enough with all the construction they're doing on Route 9. They're supposedly adding a new toll lane, but they've just had these concrete barriers up for six months and nobody is ever actually working when I drive past. It completely messed up my car's alignment a few weeks ago because I hit this massive pothole they left uncovered near the exit ramp. I had to take my car into the shop, and the mechanic—Gary, I think his name was, he always has this smudge of grease right on his nose—he tried to tell me I needed all new struts. I told him I just need the alignment done, I'm not falling for the upsell. It's like when you go to Best Buy to get a TV and they try to sell you the eighty-dollar HDMI cable. I read online that the cheap ones on Amazon do the exact same thing because it's a digital signal, it either works or it doesn't. I bought a pack of three cables for twelve bucks and they work perfectly for my dual monitor setup at work. Having two monitors is an absolute lifesaver for managing the executive calendars, honestly, I don't know how I ever did it on a single screen... 

Wait, sorry, I'm getting completely off track again. You asked about hearing things. So, yeah, I don't have any strange beliefs or see things that aren't there, it's just those random voices saying my name or telling me about the schedule when nobody is in the room.

inference.note: F34.1 was ruled out because symptoms have not persisted for 2 years. The last time I flew out of there, they lost my luggage for three days, and I was going to my cousin's wedding in Chicago. I had to buy a suit off the rack at Macy's at the last minute, and the sleeves were just a fraction too long. It drove me crazy in all the photos. 

Actually, speaking of photos, I've kind of pulled back from my photography outings. I used to go out every weekend with my DSLR, but I just don't feel as present or reliable right now. Same with my mentoring program, I've stepped back from that too. I just don't have the focus. I tried taking pictures of the cherry blossoms last month, but the lighting was all wrong, and then my battery died because I forgot to charge it. I bought this new rapid charger online, but the cord is so short I have to plug it in right next to the kitchen sink, which seems like a terrible safety hazard. My kitchen is so cramped anyway, I really need to re-tile the backsplash, but... 

Wait, what was I saying? Oh, right, how it's affecting me. Yeah, so work is mostly okay, just takes more effort, but I've definitely dropped the ball on my hobbies and mentoring stuff.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the depressive symptoms are better explained by complicated bereavement/adjustment rather than a major depressive episode, by assessing whether the brother is deceased or the stressor is a loss
doctor.question: Is your brother still alive?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking a family history question about whether my brother is still alive, which is not covered by any of the symptom profile items.

patient.answer:
Yeah, he is. He actually just turned forty-two last month. We usually go out for a steak dinner for his birthday, but this year he wanted to try this new vegan place downtown that his wife has been raving about. I guess they make these imitation crab cakes out of artichoke hearts and some kind of seaweed extract. I was really skeptical, honestly, because I love actual seafood. I grew up going to the Maryland shore every summer, and there is nothing like a real blue crab covered in Old Bay seasoning. We used to catch them right off the dock with just a piece of chicken neck tied to a string. It's crazy how simple it is, you just pull the string up really slow and scoop them with a net. 

My grandfather taught me how to do it when I was maybe six or seven. He had this old wooden boat that always smelled like diesel fuel and wet rope. He spent half his retirement just sanding and varnishing that boat. I tried to help him once, but I spilled a whole can of marine varnish on the driveway, and my grandmother was absolutely furious. She had these beautiful hydrangeas planted right next to the driveway, and she was convinced the fumes were going to kill them. Hydrangeas are so finicky anyway, you have to get the soil acidity exactly right if you want them to be blue instead of pink. I tried growing them at my place, but the soil here is mostly clay, so I gave up and just planted hostas instead. Hostas are basically indestructible, you can just... 

Wait, sorry. I'm doing it again, aren't I? You asked about my brother. Yes, he's still alive, doing fine.

Well, my sleep has been really strange lately. There have been nights when I only sleep for maybe two or three hours, and I'll wake up way before dawn. But the weird thing is, I don't even feel tired. I'll just get up and feel completely ready to start answering emails or updating the appointment lists for the executives. 

Which is actually kind of helpful, because the new email system they rolled out at work is a complete disaster. They switched us over to this cloud-based platform over the weekend, and it completely wiped out all my custom folder rules. I had everything color-coded by department—marketing was green, finance was blue, HR was yellow. It took me months to get it perfectly organized. And now, every single email just dumps right into the main inbox. It's like trying to find a needle in a haystack. I tried calling IT, but they outsource their help desk now, so you just sit on hold listening to this awful elevator music. It's that same looping jazz track that they play in the lobby of my dentist's office. 

My dentist, Dr. Aris, he has this massive saltwater fish tank in his waiting room. It's actually really relaxing to watch. He has this one clownfish that always hides inside a little plastic shipwreck. I always think about getting a fish tank, but the maintenance seems like a nightmare. You have to check the pH levels constantly, and if the filter breaks, the whole tank can go bad in a day. My neighbor had a tank and it leaked all over his hardwood floors. Ruined the oak finish, he had to have the whole living room sanded and refinished. The dust from the sanding got into his HVAC system and...

Wait, sorry, I'm wandering off again. What did you ask? Oh, right, my sleep. Yeah, so I've just been sleeping a couple of hours some nights, waking up super early, but feeling totally energized and ready to work instead of being exhausted.

doctor.intent: Differentiate a major depressive episode from a mood disorder due to a medical condition by assessing whether the mood/symptoms are better explained by a neurological or medical illness.

patient.answer:
No, I haven't had any of those things. No strokes or seizures or anything like that. I did bump my head pretty hard once on the corner of an open cabinet door in the kitchen, though. It was one of those upper cabinets, and I was trying to reach the good olive oil. I buy this specific kind imported from Italy, it comes in a tall dark green bottle. The dark glass is important because light degrades the oil faster, which ruins the flavor. I learned that from this cooking class I took at the community center a few years ago. 

The instructor was this really intense guy who used to be a sous chef at a Michelin-star restaurant in New York. He was absolutely militant about how to hold a chef's knife. He made us practice chopping celery for an entire hour during the first class. I bought a really nice Wüsthof knife after that, carbon steel, holds an edge beautifully. But you have to hand wash it immediately, you can never put it in the dishwasher. The detergent in those pods is way too abrasive, and the heat cycle can warp the handle. I actually need to get some more of those dishwasher pods, the lemon-scented ones. The regular ones leave this weird chalky residue on my water glasses, and it drives me crazy when I'm setting the table... 

Wait, what was the question? Oh, right, brain stuff. No, nothing like that, my brain is fine, no strokes or injuries.

doctor.intent: To determine whether the depressive syndrome is due to a general medical condition/other medical cause versus a primary major depressive episode

No, I haven't. I've never really felt this down before, not like this. I mean, sure, everyone gets sad sometimes, like when my cat died a few years ago. He was this big orange tabby named Marmalade. I adopted him from the shelter when he was just a kitten, and he used to sleep right on my chest every night. The shelter is actually run by this really sweet older couple who retired from teaching. They spend all their time rescuing strays and organizing these huge adoption events at the local pet store. 

The pet store is right next to this amazing bakery that makes the best sourdough bread. The secret is their starter, they claim it's over a hundred years old and came all the way from San Francisco. I tried making sourdough during the pandemic, like everyone else did, but my starter just smelled like old gym socks and never bubbled right. I think my kitchen is just too cold in the winter. The draft comes right through the window above the sink. I bought that plastic shrink-wrap stuff to seal it, but you have to use a hairdryer to get it tight, and my hairdryer just broke. The coil inside snapped and it started smoking, which was terrifying. I had to throw it out and now I have to let my hair air dry, which takes forever because...

Wait, sorry. Did I answer your question? You asked about being depressed before, right? No, I've never had a period like this before without a reason. This is the first time.

Well, honestly, I don't think they're really connected. It seems pretty independent. Like, my mood just does what it does, regardless of how he's doing. He's been doing okay lately, though. He actually just got a new car, a silver Honda Civic. It gets incredible gas mileage, which is great because gas prices are just ridiculous right now. I went to fill up my tank on Tuesday, and it was over four dollars a gallon at the station on the corner. 

That station used to be a little family-owned place where they'd actually come out and pump the gas for you, check your oil, clean your windshield. You don't see that anymore. Now it's all automated, and half the time the card readers on the pumps don't even work. You have to go inside to pay, and the line is always huge because everyone is buying lottery tickets. I don't understand the appeal of the lottery. The odds of winning are astronomically low. You have a better chance of being struck by lightning while holding a winning ticket than actually winning the jackpot. 

My uncle actually got struck by lightning once. He was out golfing in a thunderstorm, which is just about the dumbest thing you can do. He was holding a nine iron, and... wait, I'm doing it again, aren't I? 

Sorry. What were we talking about? My mood and my brother? Right. Yeah, I haven't really noticed any connection. My mood just stays low on its own, even if he's having a good week.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the mood episode includes a manic period, which would favor bipolar-related depression over a non-bipolar depressive disorder with psychotic features.

target_item.name: Elevated_Irritable_Mood

patient.answer:
Well, yeah, I do get these stretches where I feel unusually upbeat, like everything is just clicking perfectly. I'll have all this energy at work, getting through my whole inbox, scheduling everything perfectly. But then, if someone does something tiny, like moving a meeting by 15 minutes, I can get really sharp with them. It even surprises me how irritable I get over nothing. 

Speaking of meetings, my boss uses this scheduling software that is just an absolute nightmare. It's supposed to sync with everyone's calendars automatically, but half the time it double-books people or puts things in the wrong time zone. We have this one client in London, and trying to coordinate a call with them is like doing advanced calculus. London is nice, though. I went there for a week in my twenties. We stayed in this little hostel near the British Museum. The museum is incredible, they have the actual Rosetta Stone. I couldn't believe how big it was in person, and the crowds around it were just insane. Everyone trying to get a picture with their iPads. I never understood why people take pictures with iPads, they're so huge and awkward to hold up. 

My niece got an iPad for her birthday last year, the one with the Apple Pencil. She draws these amazing digital portraits on it. She's only twelve, but she's already talking about going to art school in Chicago. Chicago has great architecture, the boat tours on the river are fantastic... 

Wait, I'm losing track again. You asked if I get high or irritable? Yeah, I do have those days where I'm super upbeat and energetic, and then I just snap at people if things change.

doctor.intent: Clarify whether the elevated/energized periods meet criteria for true mania by assessing for psychosis or severe impairment, which would favor bipolar disorder with psychotic features over a depressive disorder due to another medical condition

No, no, it's never gotten that extreme. I mean, nobody's ever had to drag me to the hospital or anything like that. People might notice I'm talking a little faster or getting a bit snappy, but I don't go totally off the rails. It's just, you know, a lot of energy. 

I did have to go to the hospital once, though, but that was for my appendix. God, that was awful. It happened right in the middle of our huge quarterly review at work. I had spent three weeks preparing all the binders for the executives. We still use physical binders, can you believe that? My boss insists on it. He says he likes the tactile feel of turning the pages. He's very old school. He still wears these tweed jackets with the elbow patches, like he's a professor from the 1950s. I actually saw a jacket just like his in a vintage shop downtown last weekend. 

I love wandering around downtown on Saturdays. There's this farmer's market that sets up near the river, and they have the best local honey. I always buy a jar of the clover honey. It's supposed to be really good for allergies, though honestly, my allergies have been terrible this year regardless. The pollen count has been off the charts. My car is constantly coated in this fine yellow dust. I have to run it through the car wash twice a week, and the guys at the car wash are starting to recognize me...

Wait, sorry. No, I haven't ever been hospitalized for my mood or had people really worry about me like that. It's just the energy thing.

target_item.name: Inflated_Self_Esteem

patient.answer:
Well, yeah, sometimes I do get this feeling that I'm just... I don't know, operating on a higher level than everyone else. Like, I'll feel like I'm the only one who can actually straighten out the doctors my brother sees, keep the family in line, and fix everything at the office all at once. I start really believing that my organizational system is just flat-out better than anyone else's judgment. 

It's like this one system I designed for the filing room at work. We had these massive cabinets, the old metal ones that squeak when you pull the drawers out. I spent an entire weekend color-coding the tabs. I used those little Avery labels, you know the ones? You have to run them through the printer just right or they jam. Our office printer is constantly jamming anyway. It's a huge Xerox machine that takes up half the breakroom. 

The breakroom is a disaster, honestly. Someone always leaves their Tupperware in the fridge until it grows mold. Last week, I found a container of what I think used to be lasagna, but it looked like a science experiment. I don't get how people can be so careless with their food. My mother taught me to always label and date leftovers. She was meticulous about the kitchen. She had this set of vintage Pyrex bowls, the ones with the primary colors... 

Wait, what was I saying? Oh, right. Yeah, I just get this sense that my way of doing things is the only right way, and I'm the only one who can fix it all.

Yeah, actually. Even when I'm completely fine—like, not revved up at all, sleeping my normal amount, just having a regular, calm week—I'll still have these stretches that last for more than a couple of weeks where I hear my name being called when nobody's there. Or I'll get totally convinced that completely ordinary comments from my boss or coworkers are actually these secret, coded tests they're running on me. 

Speaking of tests, my nephew just had to take the SATs last month. He was so stressed out about it, studying every single night with these massive prep books. I remember taking the SATs back in the day. We had to use those number two pencils and fill in the little bubbles so carefully. If you didn't erase completely, the machine would mark it wrong. It's crazy how much pressure we put on kids with those standardized tests. I read an article recently that said a lot of colleges are going test-optional now anyway. 

Which honestly makes sense, because how much does a test really tell you about a person? I mean, I learned more working my first job at this little independent bookstore than I ever did in a classroom. The smell of old paper in that place was incredible. We had this huge section of first editions behind glass. The owner, Mr. Henderson, was this sweet older guy who always drank Earl Grey tea out of a chipped mug...

Wait, sorry, I'm drifting again. But yes, to answer your question, even when my mood is totally normal and steady, I've still had those voices and the feeling that people are testing me with hidden meanings for weeks at a time.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the current episode has a recent medical or substance trigger, which would support a mood disorder due to a medical condition rather than a primary bipolar or depressive disorder.

patient.answer:
No, no, I haven't been doing any of that. I don't really drink much anyway, maybe just a glass of wine at Thanksgiving or something. We always have Thanksgiving at my sister's house. She makes this incredible sweet potato casserole with the marshmallows on top. I know some people think it's too sweet, like dessert, but it's a family tradition. Our grandmother used to make it in this huge, heavy ceramic dish that had a tiny chip on one of the handles. 

My sister actually inherited that dish. She keeps it on the top shelf of her pantry because she's terrified her kids are going to break it. Her youngest, Leo, is a total hurricane. He's six now, and he just runs through the house knocking things over. Last time I was there, he knocked over a vase of fake sunflowers. I don't really get the appeal of fake flowers, honestly. They just collect dust. Real flowers are so much better, even if they don't last as long. I used to keep a real orchid on my desk at work, but the air conditioning in the office is so aggressive it just sort of wilted and died within a month. 

The maintenance guy, Dave, says he can't adjust the vents because the whole floor is on one central system. Dave's a good guy, though. He always has these crazy stories about his fishing trips up at the lake...

Wait, sorry. What did you ask me? Oh, right, drugs and alcohol. No, I haven't been using anything like that. Just my regular coffee in the morning.

doctor.intent: Assess whether the psychotic symptoms occur exclusively during mood episodes or also persist outside them, which helps distinguish bipolar disorder with psychotic features from schizoaffective disorder or primary mood disorder with psychotic features.
doctor.question: Do the voices or unusual beliefs ever happen only when your mood is not high or low, or only during those mood episodes?

target_item.name: Additional Requirement 1
target_item.manifestation: During my high-energy stretches, the certainty that messages or calendar problems meant something special would get stronger, and I would sometimes hear those short comments while I was running on very little sleep.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the temporal relationship between the psychotic symptoms and the mood episodes, specifically whether they occur concurrently during the mood episodes.

patient.answer:
Well, it's kind of a mix, honestly. Like I said, I definitely get the voices and the feeling about the secret tests even when my mood is totally steady and normal. But... when I'm in one of those high-energy stretches, you know, when I'm running on barely any sleep and fixing everything? The feeling definitely gets stronger. Like, I'll be absolutely certain that a glitch in the office calendar or a weirdly worded email is this incredibly important, special message meant just for me. And I'll sometimes hear those short comments or voices right in the middle of all that rushing around. 

Speaking of the office calendar, we just switched to this new software system last month, and it is a total nightmare. The interface is completely counterintuitive. You try to schedule a recurring meeting, and it somehow invites the entire department instead of just the three people you selected. My boss, Mr. Thompson, was furious when he got fifty decline notifications for a simple check-in meeting. He's not great with technology anyway. He still prints out all his emails to read them. He has this massive stack of paper on his desk that just keeps growing. 

I keep telling him we need to go paperless. It's better for the environment, anyway. I started recycling more at home, too. I got one of those dual trash cans with the separate compartments. It's stainless steel, looks really sleek in the kitchen. But the bags for it are so expensive. You have to buy the specific brand or they don't fit right around the rim. I tried using regular grocery bags once, but they just slipped down inside and made a huge mess with the coffee grounds. 

I drink a lot of coffee, especially when I'm on one of those high-energy kicks. I have this French press that makes the best cup... 

Oh, wait. Sorry. I'm doing it again, aren't I? But yeah, the voices and the beliefs happen when I'm normal, but they definitely get more intense and I hear the comments more when I'm in those super high-energy, no-sleep periods.

inference.note: Schizoaffective disorder, bipolar type (F25.0) is now added because psychotic symptoms occur for weeks even when mood is normal, which argues against purely mood-episode-limited psychosis. Bipolar I disorder with psychotic features (F31.2) and current manic episode without psychotic symptoms/with severe depression? retained in differential, though the persistent psychosis makes a primary psychotic-spectrum diagnosis more likely. Current major depressive episode with psychotic symptoms (F32.3) and recurrent depressive disorder with psychotic symptoms (F06.31) are ruled out by clear manic/hypomanic history.

doctor.intent: Determine whether psychotic symptoms have occurred for a substantial portion of the mood episode, which helps distinguish schizoaffective disorder from bipolar disorder with psychotic features.

patient.answer:
Yeah, like I was saying a few minutes ago, that's exactly what happens. There have been plenty of totally calm weeks where I wasn't revved up or sleeping less or anything like that, but for more than a couple of weeks straight, I still heard my name out of nowhere, or I felt completely convinced that ordinary comments from my coworkers were those coded tests. 

Speaking of coworkers and comments, we actually just had our quarterly reviews. The new HR director, Gary, sat in on them. Gary wears these incredibly loud, novelty silk ties. Last Tuesday he had one with little golfing cartoon characters all over it. I just don't understand novelty ties in a professional environment, you know? As an executive assistant, I have to look sharp, so I always take my dress shirts to this dry cleaner down the street from my apartment. But I swear, every third time I pick them up, they've broken a button. They use this massive industrial press that just crushes the plastic. I actually had to buy a little travel sewing kit just to replace the buttons myself. The needles in those kits are so tiny, though. I can barely thread them without my reading glasses, and I keep misplacing my glasses. I left them in the breakroom next to the microwave yesterday...

Wait, sorry, I lost track again. But yes, absolutely. Even when my mood is perfectly normal and stable, those voices and the coded test things have definitely lasted for two weeks or more.

I think... wait, didn't you just ask me that? Or something really similar? But yeah, like I was saying, there have definitely been calm weeks where I wasn't revved up or sleeping less or anything. final_diagnosis.reason: The patient has clear manic symptoms (decreased need for sleep, increased energy, irritability, grandiosity, distractibility/pressured rambling) and psychotic symptoms (auditory hallucinations and fixed bizarre/paranoid ideas) that are present not only during mood episodes but also for >2 weeks when mood is normal. This establishes schizoaffective disorder, bipolar type rather than bipolar disorder with psychotic features, because psychosis persists independently of mood episodes.
